stemMd: A cell placed in a solution loses water and shrinks. Assuming the membrane is permeable to water but not the dissolved solute, the external solution was initially what relative to the cell?
explanationMd: Water moves osmotically toward the compartment with the higher effective concentration of nonpenetrating solutes. Net water leaving the cell therefore indicates a hypertonic external solution. The permeability assumption matters because freely penetrating solutes may not sustain tonicity.

distractorRationale.e: A hypotonic solution would drive net water into the cell.
distractorRationale.d: Isotonic conditions do not produce this net osmotic water loss.
distractorRationale.c: Pure water would generally be hypotonic to a cell.
distractorRationale.a: Absence of solute would not explain water leaving the cell.
